facts.fact_text: On 6 May 2012 the applicant was arrested during the dispersal of a political rally at Bolotnaya Square in Moscow.
On 23 April 2012 five individuals (Mr I. Bakirov, Mr S. Davidis, Ms Y. Lukyanova, Ms N. Mityushkina and Mr S. Udaltsov) submitted notice of a public demonstration to the mayor of Moscow.
The planned march had an estimated 5,000 participants.
The planned march was to begin at 4 p.m. on 6 May 2012 from Triumfalnaya Square.
The planned march was to be followed by a meeting at Manezhnaya Square, which was to end at 8 p.m.

The aim of the demonstration was to protest against abuses and falsifications in the course of the elections to the State Duma and of the President of the Russian Federation, and to demand fair elections, respect for human rights, the rule of law and the international obligations of the Russian Federation.
On 27 April 2012 the organisers requested an alternative route from Kaluzhskaya Square, down Bolshaya Yakimanka Street and Bolshaya Polyanka Street, followed by a meeting at Bolotnaya Square.
The march was to begin at 4 p.m. and the meeting was to finish by 7.30 p.m.
The number of participants for the alternative route proposal was indicated as 5,000.
On 6 May 2012 the applicant arrived at Bolotnaya Square at around 6 p.m. to take part in the meeting.
The applicant stood in front of the stage on Bolotnaya Embankment, within the area designated as the meeting venue.
According to the applicant, between 6 p.m. and 7 p.m. the area around him remained peaceful, although there was general confusion.

On 26 April 2012 the Head of the Moscow Department of Regional Security, Mr A. Mayorov, informed the organisers that the requested route could not be allocated because of preparations for the Victory Day parade on 9 May 2012.

On 3 May 2012 the Moscow Department of Regional Security approved the alternative route from Kaluzhskaya Square, down Bolshaya Yakimanka Street and Bolshaya Polyanka Street, followed by a meeting at Bolotnaya Square.
The units assigned to Zone no. 8 were instructed to search the demonstrators to prevent them from taking camping tents to the site of the meeting.
The units assigned to Zone no. 8 were instructed to obstruct access to Bolshoy Kamennyy Bridge, diverting the marchers to Bolotnaya Embankment, the site of the meeting.
The adjacent park at Bolotnaya Square had to be cordoned off under the security plan.

The only entrance to Bolotnaya Embankment – from Malyy Kamennyy Bridge – had to be equipped with fourteen metal detectors, which were to be removed just before the march approached the site of the meeting.

The command of Zone no. 8, in particular Police Colonels Smirnov and Saprykin, were under orders to meet the organisers in person at the beginning of the event to remind them of their responsibilities and to have them sign an undertaking.
At approximately 1.30 p.m. on 6 May 2012 the organisers were allowed access to Bolotnaya Square to set up the stage and sound equipment.
Unlike on 4 February 2012, the park at Bolotnaya Square was excluded from the meeting venue on 6 May 2012, which was limited to Bolotnaya Embankment.

A cordon of riot police in full protection gear barred access to the park at Bolotnaya Square and continued along the whole perimeter of the meeting area, channelling the demonstration to Bolotnaya Embankment.
Further down Bolotnaya Embankment there was a row of metal detectors at the entrance to the meeting venue.
At 6 p.m. Police Colonel A. Makhonin told Ms N. Mityushkina to make an announcement from the stage that the meeting was over.

Ms N. Mityushkina made the announcement from the stage that the meeting was over, but apparently her message was not heard by most of the demonstrators or the media reporters broadcasting from the spot.
At 6.15 p.m., at the corner of Malyy Kamennyy Bridge, the riot police began breaking into the demonstration to split the crowd.
Running in tight formations, the riot police pushed the crowd apart, arrested some people, confronted others and formed new cordons to isolate sections of the crowd.
The police applied combat techniques and used truncheons during the dispersal at 6.15 p.m.
At 6.21 p.m. several police officers arrested Mr S. Udaltsov and took him away from the stage.
Mr A. Navalnyy attempted to go up onto the stage, but he was also arrested at the stairs and taken away.
At Malyy Kamennyy Bridge the police continued dividing the crowd and began pushing some sections away from the venue.
Through the loudspeakers the police requested that the participants leave for the metro station.
The dispersal of the demonstration continued for at least another hour until the venue was fully cleared of all protesters.

The Federal Law on assemblies, meetings, demonstrations, marches and pickets (no. FZ-54 of 19 June 2004, the Public Events Act) required that notification of a public event be filed by its organiser in writing with the executive body of the constituent entity of the Russian Federation or the municipal authorities no earlier than fifteen days and no later than ten days prior to the scheduled date of the event.

Article 19.3 of the Code of Administrative Offences of the Russian Federation provided that failure to obey a lawful order or demand of a police officer in connection with the performance of the officer's official duties relating to maintaining public order and security, or impeding the officer's performance of his or her official duties, shall be punishable by a fine of between RUB 500 and RUB 1,000 or by administrative detention for up to fifteen days.

The aim of the demonstration was to protest against abuses and falsifications in the course of the elections to the State Duma and of the President of the Russian Federation, and to demand fair elections, respect for human rights, the rule of law and the international obligations of the Russian Federation.

On 26 April 2012 the Head of the Moscow Department of Regional Security, Mr A. Mayorov, informed the organisers that the requested route could not be allocated because of preparations for the Victory Day parade on 9 May 2012.
The Moscow Department of Regional Security requested the Moscow Department of the Interior to safeguard public order in Moscow in light of the threatened unauthorised occupation of Manezhnaya Square.

The security plan provided for security measures in Moscow city centre in view of the forthcoming authorised demonstration at Bolotnaya Square and anticipated attempts by other opposition groups to hold unauthorised public gatherings.

Section 12(2) of the Public Events Act required the executive body of the constituent entity of the Russian Federation or the municipal authorities to immediately notify the organiser of the public event by issuing a reasoned written warning if the information in the notification gave grounds to suppose that the aims or conduct of the planned event did not comply with the Constitution of the Russian Federation or were in breach of prohibitions established by administrative or criminal legislation.
Unlike on 4 February 2012, the park at Bolotnaya Square was excluded from the meeting venue on 6 May 2012, which was limited to Bolotnaya Embankment.

The Expert Commission noted that the police did not inform the organisers of the changes they had decided upon, and the organisers only became aware of the police-imposed changes to the event when they arrived at the site on the afternoon of 6 May 2012.

The Expert Commission's report stated that as the march approached Bolotnaya Square, demonstrators found that a police cordon was blocking off most of the square, leaving only a narrow stretch along the waterfront for the rally.

The Expert Commission's report contained two photographs comparing the police cordon on 4 February 2012 (a thin line of police officers without protection gear) and the one on 6 May 2012 (multiple ranks of riot police with full protection gear backed up by heavy vehicles).

Mr B. Nemtsov testified that on 4 February 2012 there was an authorised event where all of Bolotnaya Square was open with no cordons on Bolshoy Kamennyy Bridge, and they were sure that on 6 May 2012 it would be exactly the same, but the police had blocked Bolotnaya Square leaving a very narrow passage for the demonstrators.
Mr B. Nemtsov testified that on the website of the Moscow Department of the Interior a map was posted showing that the park of Bolotnaya Square should have been open, but it turned out to be closed.

Ms N. Mirza testified that as she was later told by Police Colonel V. Biryukov, the protesters had sat down on the ground because the passage had been narrowed down, and she confirmed that the passage was much narrower than usual and there were metal detectors which were not supposed to be there.

The witness Ms N. Mirza testified in the proceedings against Mr S. Udaltsov and Mr Razvozzhayev that Police Colonel V. Biryukov had asked her and the Ombudsman to come to Malyy Kamennyy Bridge where some of the protesters, including Mr B. Nemtsov and Mr S. Udaltsov, had not turned right towards the stage but had gone straight to the cordon, where they had begun a sit-in protest on the pretext that access to the park of Bolotnaya Square had been closed and cordoned off.

The witness Mr I. Ponomarev testified in the proceedings against Mr S. Udaltsov and Mr Razvozzhayev that the police cordon had been placed differently from the cordon placed for the similar march on 4 February 2012, and that he proposed to Mr S. Udaltsov that the cordon be pushed back so that the police would go back a few steps and widen access to Bolotnaya Square.

The witness Mr G. Gudkov, deputy of the State Duma, testified in the proceedings against Mr S. Udaltsov and Mr Razvozzhayev that at the request of the organisers he had taken part in the negotiations with the police on moving the cordon back and opening up access to the park at Bolotnaya Square, and that he had reached an agreement with the officers of the Moscow Department of the Interior that the cordon would be moved back, but those who had called for a sit-in, including Mr S. Udaltsov, refused to go to the offices of the Moscow Department of the Interior to sign the necessary documents.

The witness Mr D. Gudkov, deputy of the State Duma, testified in the proceedings against Mr S. Udaltsov and Mr Razvozzhayev that together with Mr G. Gudkov he had conducted negotiations with the police and an agreement had been reached that the cordon at Malyy Kamennyy Bridge would be moved back and access to the park would be opened up, but at that point some young men in hoodies among the protesters began pushing citizens onto the cordon, after which the cordon broke, the police began the arrests and mass disorder ensued.
